NVIDIA CUDA inference backend for the ollama LLM server
Adds the CUDA ggml backend so a composing GPU box runs inference on an
NVIDIA card instead of falling back to CPU. This is an ADD-ON to the
ollama candy, never a replacement: it contributes only the backend
libraries that drop into ollama's own runner directory
(/usr/lib/ollama/cuda_v*/libggml-cuda.so plus the CUDA runtime it links),
which is why the base ollama candy can stay CPU-only and small ON A PACKAGED
DISTRO — on the tarball path the upstream archive already carries this backend,
so this candy asserts rather than installs. Keeping
the backend in its own candy is what makes GPU support a per-box
composition choice: an image that wants CUDA composes this, an image
that does not pays none of its ~1 GiB.

Two install paths, one assertion. On Arch (CachyOS included) the split
`ollama-cuda` package supplies the backend — it depends on the `ollama`
package, so the two compose rather than conflict. On a distro that has no
ollama package the base candy installs the upstream tarball, which already
bundles the CUDA backend, so this candy adds no package there and simply
asserts the backend really is present. Either way the check below fails
when the CUDA backend is missing, which is the property worth having.
